rules.title: Prohibition on sale/provision of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_text: All residential dwelling units in Berkeley; applies to vendors/providers of coordinated pricing algorithms. Definition excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable housing limit products, and market research/appraisal/software development research uses.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.penalty: City Attorney civil action: damages, injunctive relief, restitution, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees (BMC 13.63.040(A)).
rules.ambiguity_note: Ordinance passed to print November 18, 2025 (document is a Dec 2, 2025 agenda item); effective date not stated in text; status assumed in force.

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Each month of violation and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, damages, injunctive relief, restitution; tenants may sue and recover attorney's fees (BMC 13.63.040).
rules.ambiguity_note: Ordinance passed to print November 18, 2025 (document is a Dec 2, 2025 agenda item); effective date not stated in text; status assumed in force.

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – criminal history prohibitions
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions. Prohibited acts include refusing to rent or terminating a tenancy, requiring disclosure, demanding a higher deposit or rent, refusing to add a family member, and disqualifying tenants from rental assistance programs, based on criminal history.
rules.coverage_text: Rental housing providers in Berkeley with regard to current or prospective tenants, subject to listed exemptions.
rules.exemptions_text: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record resides in one unit as primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owner move-back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.

exemption_tests.description: Lifetime sex offenders
Public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions
Owner-occupied properties (1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as primary residence
Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home per BMC 13.76.130 A.9
Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.ambiguity_note: Text states the Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; an effective date is not stated.

rules.title: Fair Chance – written notice and opportunity to respond
rules.requirement: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history, the landlord must give written notice and an opportunity to respond. Housing providers must also post the City's Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants on application materials, websites, and locations frequently visited by applicants.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords in Berkeley taking action against applicants or tenants based on criminal history, subject to ordinance exemptions.
rules.exemptions_text: Same exemptions as the Fair Chance Ordinance; see ordinance for specifics.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied properties (1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one unit as primary residence

rules.quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, plus civil damages and other remedies.
rules.ambiguity_note: Effective date not stated; exemption applicability to this requirement is assumed from the page's general exemption list.

rules.title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance (2026 inflation-adjusted amounts)
rules.requirement: Owners must pay tenants relocation assistance when evicting for an owner move-in. Effective January 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413, with an additional $6,471 for qualifying households, indexed annually to CPI.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted for an owner move-in under the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; coverage details not stated on this page.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (2026 Adjustments of Relocation Assistance Payments, Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.
rules.ambiguity_note: News page summarizing an annual adjustment; underlying ordinance section numbers and coverage/exemptions are not stated.

rules.title: Ellis Act eviction relocation assistance (2026 inflation-adjusted amounts)
rules.requirement: Owners removing a property from the rental market must pay tenants the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions, indexed annually to inflation: $19,413 standard and $6,471 additional for qualifying households from January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted so the owner can remove the property from the rental housing market under the Ellis Implementation Ordinance; coverage details not stated.
rules.citation: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance (2026 Adjustments of Relocation Assistance Payments, Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.
rules.ambiguity_note: News page summarizing an annual adjustment; underlying ordinance section numbers and coverage/exemptions are not stated.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee rights statement and fee cap disclosure
rules.requirement: An owner or agent who charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and process a rental application must give applicants, in the application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.coverage_text: Owners or agents of residential rental property in Berkeley who charge an application/screening fee.
rules.key_value: Maximum 2026 screening fee stated on page: $68.96 (state cap under Civ. Code 1950.6)
rules.quoted_span:
When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)
rules.ambiguity_note: Page notes the URL for the rights statement is yet to be provided by the City.

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners or agents may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents, as to existing tenants.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5%
rules.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA) allowed for fully covered units is set by a CPI-based formula but may not exceed 5% in any year. Landlords with banked AGAs may still raise rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.coverage_text: Fully covered units under the Rent Ordinance (e.g., most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; also certain government-owned or subsidized units).
rules.exemptions_text: Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to the rent ceiling/AGA.

exemption_tests.description: Partially covered units (e.g., new construction with certificate of occupancy after 1980, most single-family homes and condominiums) are not subject to the rent ceiling.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.ambiguity_note: Page does not state an exact effective date for the cap.

rules.title: Government-owned or -subsidized units now subject to rent ceiling
rules.requirement: Government-owned or -subsidized units registered as fully covered have a rent ceiling, so rent increases are limited by the Annual General Adjustment. Whether a unit is fully or partially covered depends on unit type and on whether federal/state law or regulation exempts it from rent control.
rules.coverage_text: Units with subsidies such as Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME, etc., that are fully covered by unit type.
rules.exemptions_text: Section 202, Section 811, and HUD-insured/held project subsidies are only partially covered because federal/state law prohibits rent control.

exemption_tests.description: Units with Section 202 or Section 811 subsidies, or certain HUD-insured projects (Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside, Project-based Section 8), are only partially covered.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span:
Units that are fully covered will have a rent ceiling, meaning rent increases will be limited by the
Annual General Adjustment
set by the Rent Board each year.

rules.title: Just cause required for eviction of covered tenants
rules.requirement: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is just cause (previously called good cause).
rules.coverage_text: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions_text: Exempt units (e.g., shared kitchen/bath with a landlord who lived on the property before the tenant) are not covered.

exemption_tests.description: Units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with a landlord who resided on the same property at the start of the tenancy are exempt.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).

rules.title: Nonpayment eviction requires debt of at least one month's Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for nonpayment only if the tenant owes rental debt equal to or greater than one month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont metro FMR) for a unit of equivalent size, for the fiscal year in which rent is demanded.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in fully or partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.key_value: Rental debt >= one month HUD FMR

rules.title: No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in fully or partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.title: Limits on eviction for violation of a material lease term
rules.requirement: Eviction for breach of a material lease term requires that the term be mutually agreed upon, that the violation cause substantial actual damage to the landlord, and that the tenant's behavior be unreasonable. The prior notice to stop must specify the lease term and describe the violation and harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in fully or partially covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span:
The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord.
The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.

rules.title: Security deposit interest under Berkeley Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords of units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.key_value: Interest paid annually; prorated on move-out
rules.ambiguity_note: Page is a summary; interest rate and calculation are on a separate page not included here.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (Security Deposits | Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) of 1.0%
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026. The AGA equals 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase for July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025 (1.5%); Regulation 1148 sets qualifying conditions and tenant notice.
rules.coverage_text: Eligible landlords of units subject to Berkeley rent stabilization; the AGA may not adjust rents of tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rents were set under Costa-Hawkins.

exemption_tests.description: 2026 AGA may not adjust rents of tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

rules.exemptions_text: The 2026 AGA may not adjust tenants' rents when their tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025, and who had their rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

rules.quoted_span:
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy – criminal history limits
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not impose blanket denials based on arrests or convictions and must review applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, judicially relieved convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old in determining eligibility or considering eviction.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.

exemption_tests.description: Policy does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others.
Guidance does not apply to current criminal behavior.

rules.exemptions_text: Not applicable where direct relationship between conviction and housing sought or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others; current criminal behavior; conflicting federal/state law preempts.

The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing    
applications.

rules.requirement: Credit history may only be used to determine ability to pay when rental history is unavailable; lack of credit history is not sufficient justification to reject an applicant, and ability to pay must be shown through identifiable income and prior rental history.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units.

rules.title: Rental assistance (Section 8 voucher) discrimination prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters based on rental assistance, including refusing to accept Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers.
rules.coverage_text: Text says it is illegal to discriminate when renting any housing in the City of Boston; no unit-count or age limits stated.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section
8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary web page; no formal ordinance or section cite, and exemptions are not described.

rules.title: Limits on considering criminal history and blanket bans in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice matters, and may not impose blanket bans on all people with a criminal history.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers covered by FEHA (landlords, property managers, tenant screening companies and others) screening rental applicants.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; does not cite the specific statute or effective date.

rules.title: Denial based on criminal conviction must be directly related to tenancy
rules.requirement: A housing provider denying an application based on a criminal conviction must show the conviction is directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and not a threat to health and safety of others or property, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers covered by FEHA screening rental applicants.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: If a housing provider intends to deny someone’s application based on a criminal conviction, it must be directly-related to someone’s ability to be a good tenant and to not be a threat to the health and safety of others and the property.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; no statute cited.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibited (including Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on a tenant's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, and must comply with paperwork requirements of rental assistance programs. Advertising such as 'No Section 8' is also prohibited.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers covered by FEHA.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; no statute cited.

rules.title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service animals and emotional support animals
rules.requirement: Tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for service animals or emotional-support animals.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants with service animals or emotional-support animals as a disability accommodation.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: Service animals and emotional-support animals are not subject to breed, size, or weight restrictions ordinarily applied to pets, and tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; no statute cited.

rules.title: Unlawful use or distribution of common pricing algorithm as part of a restraint of trade
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (a methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce.
rules.coverage_text: Any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm for products or services generally; the text does not mention rental housing specifically.
rules.exemptions_text: Definition of person excludes the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (added by Stats. 2025, ch. 338 (AB 325))
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.penalty: Violation of the Cartwright Act (punishable as a crime per the digest; enforced under the Act).
rules.ambiguity_note: General antitrust statute, not rental-specific. Chaptered Oct 6, 2025; the text does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Unlawful coercion to adopt common pricing algorithm recommendations
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a price or commercial term recommended by the algorithm for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.coverage_text: Any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm for products or services generally; the text does not mention rental housing specifically.
rules.exemptions_text: Definition of person excludes the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (added by Stats. 2025, ch. 338 (AB 325))
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
rules.ambiguity_note: General antitrust statute, not rental-specific. Chaptered Oct 6, 2025; the text does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Statewide just cause required to terminate tenancy after 12 months
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written termination notice. Just cause is either at-fault (e.g., nonpayment, breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity) or no-fault (owner move-in, withdrawal from market, government orders, demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property where tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months (24 months if adult tenants were added before 24 months, unless all tenants 12+ months or one 24+ months); excludes listed exempt housing and property under local just cause ordinances.
rules.exemptions_text: Not applicable to transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care or licensed care facilities; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner; single-family owner-occupied residences; owner-occupied duplexes; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property with non-corporate/non-REIT owner and notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; property subject to local just cause ordinances.

exemption_tests.description: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy (subd. (e)(1)).
Housing accommodations in a nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, licensed residential care facility for the elderly, or adult residential facility (e)(2).
Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school (e)(3).
Housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with an owner who maintains their principal residence at the property (e)(4).
Single-family owner-occupied residences, including residences where owner rents no more than two units or bedrooms (including ADU/JADU), and mobilehomes owned by occupant (e)(5).

Property with two separate dwelling units in a single structure where the owner occupied one unit as principal residence at the start of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU/JADU (e)(6).
Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless a mobilehome (e)(7). Rolling 15-year new-construction exemption.

Residential real property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, where owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and tenants were given the required written exemption notice (e)(8).
Housing restricted by deed, regulatory agreement or recorded document as affordable to very low, low or moderate income households, or subject to housing subsidy agreements (e)(9).
Property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or a more protective local ordinance adopted/amended after that date (i)(1).
Homeowner of a mobilehome as defined in Section 798.9 (l).

rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.key_value: 12 months occupancy (24 months if adult tenants added)
rules.penalty: Notice void; owner liable for actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x actual damages if willful, punitive damages; AG/city attorney/county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.ambiguity_note: Section amended effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1529); text states it became operative April 1, 2024 and is repealed as of January 1, 2030.

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault just cause terminations
rules.requirement: When terminating for no-fault just cause, the owner must either pay relocation assistance equal to one month's rent within 15 calendar days of service of notice or waive the final month's rent, and must state this right in the notice. Failure to strictly comply voids the termination notice.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies subject to the just cause requirement of § 1946.2(a) where the owner issues a no-fault termination notice.
rules.exemptions_text: Same exemptions as § 1946.2(e) and (i); tenant at fault for government/court order conditions is not entitled to relocation assistance.

exemption_tests.description: Section 1946.2 exemptions apply (new construction under 15 years, owner-occupied, affordable housing, local ordinance, etc.).

rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.penalty: Notice of termination void if owner fails to strictly comply.
rules.ambiguity_note: Section operative April 1, 2024 per subd. (m); amended effective 2026-01-01.

rules.title: Owner move-in and substantial remodel conditions and notice contents
rules.requirement: Owner-occupancy terminations require the intended occupant to move in within 90 days and live there at least 12 consecutive months, otherwise the unit must be offered back at same rent plus moving expenses. Demolition/substantial remodel terminations require notice with permit copies, description, and re-rent statement, and the remodel must require vacating for at least 30 consecutive days.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies subject to § 1946.2 terminated for owner move-in or demolition/substantial remodel.
rules.exemptions_text: Same as § 1946.2(e) and (i).

exemption_tests.description: Section 1946.2 exemptions apply.

rules.quoted_span: Clause (i) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the rental unit within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the rental unit as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months.
rules.key_value: 90 days to move in; 12 consecutive months occupancy; 30 consecutive days vacated for remodel
rules.penalty: Owner must re-offer unit at same rent and reimburse moving expenses; liable under subd. (h) for material violations.

rules.title: Required notice to tenants of rent limit and just cause rights
rules.requirement: Owners of property subject to the section must give tenants a written notice in at least 12-point type with prescribed language about rent limits and just cause protections, in the lease, an addendum, or a signed notice.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to § 1946.2.
rules.exemptions_text: Same as § 1946.2(e) and (i).

exemption_tests.description: Section 1946.2 exemptions apply.

rules.quoted_span: The notification or lease provision shall be in no less than 12-point type, and shall include the following:
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with any provision renders the written termination notice void.

rules.title: Statewide residential rent cap (Tenant Protection Act)
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not increase the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. No more than two increments within 12 months for the same tenant; initial rent on a new tenancy is not capped.
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including mobilehome park units), except exempt categories; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt.

exemption_tests.description: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households
Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school
Housing subject to local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap
Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless mobilehome)

Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit (e.g., single-family homes, condos) where owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and written notice of exemption is given
Property with two separate dwelling units in a single structure where the owner occupies one as principal residence at start of tenancy and continues to occupy, and neither unit is an ADU or JADU
Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome

rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to affordable/subsidized housing, dormitories, housing under stricter local rent control, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years, separately alienable property with non-corporate owner and notice, owner-occupied duplexes, and mobilehome homeowners.
rules.key_value: Lower of 5% + CPI change or 10% per 12 months
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, damages for excess rent, attorney's fees, and up to three times damages if willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious; enforcement by AG, city attorney or county counsel.
rules.ambiguity_note: Operative April 1, 2024; repealed as of January 1, 2030. Rent increases subject to the cap apply on or after March 15, 2019 (Feb 18, 2021 for mobilehome tenancies).
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Security deposit cap: one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security exceeding one month's rent (in addition to first month's rent paid on or before initial occupancy), subject to listed exceptions. Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.

exemption_tests.description: Small landlords (natural person/LLC of natural persons owning no more than two properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent instead (para. (c)(5)).
Advance payment of not less than six months' rent permitted if lease term is six months or longer.
Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

rules.exemptions_text: Paragraphs (2), (3), (5) exceptions; subdivision does not apply to security collected before July 1, 2024.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Two-month security cap for small landlords
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person (or LLC of natural persons) owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units in total may not demand or receive security exceeding two months' rent. This does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member, and the landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of it.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords who are natural persons or LLCs whose members are all natural persons and who own no more than two rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.

exemption_tests.description: Does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member (cap reverts to one month).

rules.exemptions_text: Subparagraph (A) shall not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements:
rules.ambiguity_note: Effective date inferred from paragraph (c)(6) (subdivision does not apply to security collected before July 1, 2024).

rules.title: Written explanation for higher security charged to service members
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher than standard or advertised security due to credit, housing history or similar factors, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and reason on or before lease signing, and return the additional amount after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.coverage_text: Service members renting residential property in which they will reside.
rules.quoted_span:
The additional amount of security shall be returned to the tenant after no more than six months of residency if the tenant
is not in arrears for any rent due during that period.
rules.key_value: Return of additional security after no more than 6 months

rules.title: Security held for tenant; priority over creditors
rules.requirement: Security must be held by the landlord for the tenant, and the tenant's claim to it is prior to the claim of any creditor of the landlord.
rules.coverage_text: Security for residential rental agreements.
rules.quoted_span: Any security shall be held by the landlord for the tenant who is party to the lease or agreement. The claim of a tenant to the security shall be prior to the claim of any creditor of the landlord.

rules.title: Limits on deductions from security
rules.requirement: A landlord may claim only amounts reasonably necessary for the purposes in subdivision (b) and may not claim for pre-existing damage, ordinary wear and tear, or unnecessary professional cleaning.
rules.coverage_text: Security for residential rental agreements.
rules.quoted_span:
the landlord
may claim of the security only those amounts as are reasonably necessary for the purposes specified in subdivision (b).

rules.title: Initial inspection before move-out
rules.requirement: Landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection, conduct it on request (no earlier than two weeks before termination, with 48 hours' notice), and give an itemized statement of proposed deductions so the tenant can remedy deficiencies.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security.

exemption_tests.description: Does not apply when tenancy is terminated under Code Civ. Proc. § 1161 subdivision (2), (3), or (4).

rules.exemptions_text: Requirements do not apply when tenancy terminated pursuant to CCP 1161(2), (3), or (4).
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.
rules.key_value: 48 hours' notice; no earlier than two weeks before end

rules.title: Photographs of unit at move-in and move-out
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, landlord must photograph the unit at or immediately before tenancy inception. Beginning April 1, 2025, landlord must photograph the unit after possession is returned and after repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security.
rules.quoted_span:
For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the
inception of, the tenancy.
rules.ambiguity_note: Move-out photograph requirement begins April 1, 2025; move-in photograph requirement applies to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.title: Return of security and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and disposition of the security and return any remainder, with supporting documentation for repair/cleaning charges.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security.

exemption_tests.description: Itemization documentation not required if deductions for repairs and cleaning do not exceed $125 or tenant validly waived, unless tenant requests documentation within 14 days.

rules.exemptions_text: Paragraph (2)/(3) documentation not required if deductions do not exceed $125 or tenant waived.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:
rules.penalty: Landlord not entitled to claim any amount of the security if in bad faith fails to comply with subdivision (h).

rules.title: Transfer of security upon termination of landlord's interest
rules.requirement: On termination of the landlord's interest, the landlord must within a reasonable time either transfer the remaining security to the successor and notify the tenant, or return it to the tenant with an accounting; successors are jointly liable on noncompliance.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security.
rules.quoted_span: Transfer the portion of the security remaining after any lawful deductions are made under subdivision (e) to the landlord’s successor in interest.

rules.title: Statutory damages for bad faith retention of security
rules.requirement: Bad faith claim or retention of security (or bad faith demand for replacement security) may subject the landlord or successors to statutory damages of up to twice the security amount plus actual damages.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security.
rules.quoted_span: The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
rules.key_value: Up to 2x security plus actual damages
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages
rules.ambiguity_note: Text of subdivision (m) is cut off at end of chunk.

rules.title: Bad faith retention of security deposit – statutory damages
rules.requirement: A landlord or successor in interest who in bad faith claims or retains a security deposit in violation of the section, or in bad faith demands replacement of security, may be liable for statutory damages of up to twice the deposit in addition to actual damages. The landlord bears the burden of proof as to the reasonableness of amounts claimed.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords and successors in interest subject to the security deposit section; scope not restated in this chunk.
rules.key_value: Statutory damages up to 2x the security, plus actual damages
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages
rules.quoted_span: The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Ban on 'nonrefundable' security provisions
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not contain a provision characterizing any security as 'nonrefundable.'
rules.coverage_text: Any lease or rental agreement subject to the security deposit section.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: An application screening fee may not exceed the landlord's actual out-of-pocket costs plus reasonable value of time, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI from Jan 1, 1998).
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors/cosigners.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge an application screening fee if they know or should have known that no rental unit is or will soon be available.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords of residential rental property and their agents.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Conditions for charging a screening fee (first-come process or refund)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if, when collecting it, they offer either a first-come, first-qualified screening process (with written criteria, fee only when application is considered, refund of inadvertent collections within 7 days) or a process refunding the entire fee to non-selected applicants within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application, whichever is first.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords of residential rental property and their agents.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

rules.title: Itemized receipt for screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord must provide the applicant, personally or by mail (or email if agreed), a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords of residential rental property and their agents.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

rules.title: Return of unused screening fee
rules.requirement: If the landlord does not perform a personal reference check or obtain a consumer credit report, they must return any part of the fee not used for authorized purposes.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords of residential rental property and their agents.
rules.quoted_span:
If the landlord or their agent does
not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, the landlord or their agent shall return any amount of the screening fee that is not used for the purposes authorized by this section to the applicant.

rules.title: Copy of consumer credit report to applicant
rules.requirement: If a screening fee was paid, the landlord must give the applicant a copy of their consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords of residential rental property and their agents.
rules.quoted_span: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.

rules.title: Aggregate income of unmarried co-residents must be treated like married couples
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use a financial or income standard in renting housing that fails to count the aggregate income of persons residing or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married persons.
rules.coverage_text: Rental of housing generally under the section; no unit-count or age limits stated.
rules.quoted_span:
To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income
of married persons residing together or proposing to reside together.

rules.title: Income standard for subsidized tenants must be based on tenant's portion of rent
rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use a financial or income standard for rental eligibility that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Rentals in which there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.key_value: Income standard based on tenant's portion of rent
rules.quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: Alternative evidence of ability to pay in lieu of credit history for subsidized rentals
rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a housing provider using credit history in the application process must offer the applicant the option of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent, give reasonable time to respond, and reasonably consider that evidence in lieu of credit history.
rules.coverage_text: Rentals in which there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not limit an owner's ability to request information to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity.
rules.quoted_span:
Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

rules.title: Annual rent increase cap: lesser of 5% or CPI change
rules.requirement: At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not request or receive an increase greater than the lesser of 5% or the CPI percentage change. Only one such increase is allowed in any twelve-month period regardless of the number of tenants.
rules.coverage_text: All dwelling units as defined in § 155-1, except those exempted under § 155-2.
rules.ambiguity_note: Section was amended 2-1-2023 by Ord. No. B-532; the original effective date is not stated in this text.
rules.exemptions_text: Motels/hotels; newly constructed dwellings on first rental; industrial; nonresidential/commercial; school-owned student housing; government-owned housing; buildings vacant since 1/1/1984; multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 for a limited period under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1.

exemption_tests.description: Motels and hotels
Newly constructed dwellings rented for the first time (initial rent only; must be registered before first rental)
Industrial property
Nonresidential and commercial units (apartment units in mixed buildings remain covered)
Housing provided for students by a school, college or similar institution that owns or controls it
Housing owned and operated by other government agencies
Building completely vacant on and since January 1, 1984 (initial rent only; must be registered)

Multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987, exempt for the shorter of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years (30 years if no mortgage), if landlord complied with N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq.

rules.quoted_span:
At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord
may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage
difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination
of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

rules.title: Rents controlled at October 1, 1985 base rent; excess increases void
rules.requirement: Rents are controlled at the base rent level as of October 1, 1985, and no increases may be demanded, paid or accepted except as the chapter allows. Increases in excess of those allowed are null and void and must be refunded or credited to the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: All dwelling units to which the chapter applies (§ 155-2).
rules.key_value: Base rent as of October 1, 1985 plus permitted increases
rules.ambiguity_note: Section amended 3-2-2011, 2-1-2023 and 10-22-2025; original effective date not stated.
rules.exemptions_text: Same exemptions as § 155-2.

exemption_tests.description: Motels and hotels
Newly constructed dwellings on first rental
Industrial and nonresidential/commercial property
School-owned student housing
Government-owned and operated housing
Building vacant since January 1, 1984
Multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 for a limited period under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1

rules.quoted_span:
All rents for rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this act is applicable
are hereby controlled at the base rent level received by the landlord as of October 1, 1985, and
no rental increases shall be hereinafter demanded, paid or accepted, except as provided in this
chapter.

rules.title: Rent increases only at lease expiration or termination
rules.requirement: A rent increase at any time other than lease expiration or termination of a periodic lease is void, as is any increase above what the chapter authorizes.
rules.coverage_text: Housing space in dwellings to which the chapter applies.
rules.exemptions_text: Same exemptions as § 155-2.

exemption_tests.description: Exemptions listed in § 155-2 (hotels, new construction on first rental, government/student housing, post-1987 multiple dwellings for a limited period, etc.)

rules.quoted_span:
Any rental
increase at a time other than at the expiration of a lease or termination of the periodic lease shall
be void. Any rental increase in excess of that authorized by the provisions of this chapter shall be
void.

rules.title: 30-day written notice of rent increase with reasons
rules.requirement: A landlord seeking a rent increase must give the tenant written notice at least 30 days before the effective date and explain in detail the reason for the increase.
rules.coverage_text: Dwellings to which the chapter applies.
rules.exemptions_text: Same exemptions as § 155-2.

exemption_tests.description: Exemptions listed in § 155-2

rules.quoted_span:
Any landlord
seeking an increase shall notify the tenant, in writing, at least 30 days prior to the effective date of
the increase and explain, in detail, the reason for the increase.

rules.title: Proof of previous rent paid required to register or impose increase
rules.requirement: A landlord seeking to register, impose a rent increase, or establish a legal rent must provide documented proof of prior actual rent paid. If proof is inadequate, the Rent Regulation Officer must deny the increase, and the landlord has 30 days to cure.
rules.coverage_text: Dwelling units covered by the chapter.
rules.quoted_span:
Every landlord seeking to register, impose a rent increase, or
establish a legal rent for a dwelling unit must provide documented proof of prior, actual rent
that was paid for that unit.

rules.title: Legal rent cannot exceed rent actually charged; only ordinary annual increases
rules.requirement: If a legal rent calculation exceeds the rent currently charged, the landlord may not charge the calculated higher rent. The legal rent is set at the actual rent charged, and the landlord is limited to the increases ordinarily permitted by the chapter.
rules.coverage_text: Dwelling units covered by the chapter.
rules.quoted_span:
Under no
circumstances shall a tenant be subject to an increase of rent greater than the rent that
has been charged plus properly imposed increases under this chapter based upon a legal
rent calculation that is greater than rent actually charged.

rules.title: Municipal tax surcharge on rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may seek a rent surcharge only for municipal property tax increases above the acquisition-year (or 1988) assessment, in an amount set by the Rent Regulation Officer under an approved formula. It is paid in 12 equal monthly payments, lasts 12 months, requires reapplication, may be imposed only at lease commencement or renewal, and requires registered units.
rules.quoted_span:
The rental increase permitted for taxes is determined by the Rent
Regulation Officer pursuant to a formula approved by the Rent Control Board.
rules.key_value: Tax surcharge per Rent Control Board formula; 12-month duration; paid 1/12 monthly
rules.penalty: Fine up to $2,000 per violation under § 155-21
rules.coverage_text: Rent-controlled rental units in Hoboken for which landlord applies for tax surcharge; coverage scope defined elsewhere in chapter.
rules.ambiguity_note: Section numbering in the extracted text is garbled; chunk begins mid-section.

rules.title: Water and sewerage surcharge
rules.requirement: A landlord may seek a surcharge only for municipal water and sewer charge increases above 1996 levels, in an amount determined by the Rent Regulation Officer under an approved formula, paid in 12 equal monthly payments and not counted as rent for cost-of-living increases.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may seek a water and sewerage surcharge from a tenant because of an increase
in the municipal water and sewer charges in excess of those assessed for 1996.
rules.key_value: Increase above 1996 water/sewer charges, 12 equal monthly payments
rules.penalty: Fine up to $2,000 per violation under § 155-21
rules.coverage_text: Rent-controlled tenants in Hoboken; scope defined elsewhere in chapter.
rules.ambiguity_note: Text layout places this paragraph under heading § 155-8, but it concerns the § 155-6.1 water and sewerage surcharge.

rules.title: Capital improvement surcharge cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not impose a capital improvement rent surcharge without Board approval. The surcharge is prorated over the improvement's useful life, and base rents may not rise more than 33 1/3% due to a capital improvement surcharge in any twelve-month period.
rules.quoted_span:
In making
this determination, the Board shall consider the nature and the cost of the improvement and the
effect that the proration of the surcharge shall have on the existing base rents, it being the intent
of this chapter that the base rents shall under no circumstances be increased by an amount greater
than 33 1/3% due to a capital improvement surcharge in any one twelve-month period.
rules.penalty: Fine up to $2,000 per violation under § 155-21
rules.coverage_text: Rent-controlled units in Hoboken; scope defined elsewhere in chapter.

rules.title: Capital improvement cost allowance for code violation work
rules.requirement: When computing the cost of a capital improvement, only 60% of the cost is allowed if the work eliminates violations of housing code provisions enacted after January 1, 1985.
rules.quoted_span:
For the purpose of computing the cost of a capital improvement under this section, only 60%
of the cost shall be allowed if it is for the purpose of eliminating violations of housing code
provisions, which provisions were enacted subsequent to January 1, 1985.
rules.coverage_text: Capital improvement surcharge applications for rent-controlled units.

rules.title: Hardship rental increase requires Board approval
rules.requirement: A landlord who cannot meet operating expenses or earn a fair return may apply for a hardship increase, but may not impose any increase under the Article without Board approval and prior notice to tenants at least 20 days before hearing.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall impose upon any tenant an increase in rent under this
Article without first obtaining approval with the Board.
rules.key_value: Board approval required; 20 days' notice before hearing
rules.penalty: Fine up to $2,000 per violation under § 155-21
rules.coverage_text: Rent-controlled units in Hoboken; scope defined elsewhere in chapter.

rules.title: Rent control: no rents above authorized levels
rules.requirement: No landlord may charge rents in excess of what was received on the chapter's effective date, or on January 11, 1973 if that excess is above the rent authorized by the chapter.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall, after the effective date of this chapter, charge any rents in excess of what he was
receiving from the effective date of this chapter;
rules.key_value: Rents frozen at base levels except as authorized by the chapter
rules.penalty: Fine up to $2,000 per violation; each unit and each demand/payment is a separate violation (§ 155-21)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to Hoboken rent control; scope and exemptions defined elsewhere in the chapter.

rules.title: Certificate of compliance required for regular rent increase
rules.requirement: A landlord seeking a regular rent increase under § 155-5 must include in the notice a certification of substantial compliance with building, housing, fire and property maintenance codes. Without it the notice is invalid and the tenant may refuse to pay the increase.
rules.quoted_span:
If a notice of rental increase should be served
without a certificate of substantial compliance, then that notice shall be invalid.
rules.penalty: Fine up to $2,000 per violation under § 155-21
rules.coverage_text: Rent increases under § 155-5 in Hoboken.
rules.ambiguity_note: Date is from the amendment note (Ord. No. R-449), not necessarily original enactment.

rules.title: Rent control – rent ceiling
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge rents above what they were receiving on the chapter's effective date, nor above what they received on January 11, 1973 if that excess is more than the chapter authorizes.
rules.coverage_text: Dwellings subject to Hoboken Chapter 155 (rent control); exemptions are not in this chunk.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall, after the effective date of this chapter, charge any rents in excess of what he was
receiving from the effective date of this chapter; nor shall such landlord charge any rents in excess
of what he was receiving on January 11, 1973, if such excess is in excess of the rental which is
authorized by this chapter.
rules.key_value: Rent frozen at base rent except increases authorized by chapter

rules.title: Certificate of compliance required for regular rent increase
rules.requirement: A notice of regular rent increase must include a certification of substantial compliance with the building, housing, fire and property maintenance codes. Without it the notice is invalid and the tenant may refuse to pay the increase.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of dwellings subject to Chapter 155 seeking a regular increase under § 155-5.
rules.quoted_span:

rules.quoted_span: No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent or a security deposit in excess of the amount allowed by this section.

rules.title: Security deposit receipt and statement of condition
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent receiving a security deposit must give a signed receipt, and must furnish a separate written statement of the premises' condition listing existing damage, with a prescribed notice, within ten days after tenancy commencement or upon receipt, whichever is later.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors accepting security deposits for residential premises.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.key_value: Statement of condition within 10 days of tenancy start
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.

rules.title: Security deposit record-keeping
rules.requirement: Every lessor accepting a security deposit must maintain records of damage, repairs, receipts and statements of condition, make them available for tenant inspection, and keep them for two years after the tenancy ends.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors accepting security deposits.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.quoted_span: The lessor or his agent shall maintain said record for each dwelling unit or premises for which a security deposit was accepted for a period of two years from the date of termination of the tenancy or occupancy upon which the security deposit was conditioned.
rules.penalty: Tenant entitled to immediate return of deposit and accrued interest upon wrongful failure to make record available.

rules.title: Separate interest-bearing account for security deposits
rules.requirement: Security deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing bank account in Massachusetts beyond creditors' claims, not commingled with lessor assets, and the tenant must receive a receipt with bank details within 30 days.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors holding residential security deposits.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.
rules.penalty: Failure entitles tenant to immediate return of the security deposit.

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: A lessor holding a deposit for one year or longer must pay the tenant interest at 5% per year or the lesser amount actually received from the bank, annually, with a yearly statement.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors holding security deposits for one year or longer.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser bank interest
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

rules.title: Interest and receipt for last month's rent paid in advance
rules.requirement: A lessor receiving last month's rent in advance must give a detailed receipt and pay the tenant interest at 5% per year or the lesser amount received from the bank.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors receiving last month's rent in advance.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.quoted_span: Any lessor or his agent who receives said rent in advance for the last month of tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held.
rules.penalty: Treble the interest owed plus court costs and reasonable attorneys fees if unpaid within 30 days after termination.

rules.title: Return of security deposit and permitted deductions
rules.requirement: The lessor must return the deposit or balance within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Deductions are allowed only for unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax escalation increases, and reasonable repair of tenant-caused damage (excluding normal wear and tear), supported by a sworn itemized list.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies where a security deposit is held.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;  provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following:
rules.penalty: See subsections (6) and (7): forfeiture of right to retain deposit; treble damages plus interest, costs and attorney's fees.

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit to successor in interest
rules.requirement: When a lessor transfers interest in the unit, the deposit with accrued interest must be transferred to the successor, who must notify the tenant in writing within 45 days and becomes liable for its return.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors holding security deposits who transfer their interest.
rules.exemptions_text: Granting a mortgage is not a transfer; liability does not apply to cities/towns acquiring title under chapter 60 or certain foreclosing mortgagees. Vacation rentals of 100 days or less excluded.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.
Successor-liability exemption for cities/towns acquiring title under chapter sixty and chartered financial institution foreclosing mortgagees or mortgagees in possession.

rules.quoted_span: The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such security deposit that such security deposit was transferred to him and that he is holding said security deposit.

rules.title: Forfeiture and treble damages for security deposit violations
rules.requirement: A lessor forfeits the right to retain any deposit portion for failing to comply with specified requirements (account, itemized list, successor transfer, timely return, conflicting lease terms). For certain violations the tenant is awarded three times the deposit plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential premises holding security deposits.
rules.exemptions_text: Vacation/recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.penalty: Forfeiture of deposit retention rights; treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees.

rules.title: Non-waiver of security deposit and last month's rent protections
rules.requirement: Any lease provision that conflicts with Section 15B, and any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of its provisions, is void and unenforceable as against public policy.
rules.coverage_text: All leases, rentals, occupancies and tenancies subject to Section 15B, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

exemption_tests.description: Leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less that are for a vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.exemptions_text: Section does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which is for a vacation or recreational purpose.
rules.quoted_span: Any provision of a lease which conflicts with any provision of this section and any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of this section shall be deemed to be against public policy and therefore void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Lessors barred from charging application or other fees beyond first, last, security deposit and lock change
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord (lessor) may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit, and a lock fee. Application, screening, pet, cleaning, amenity and similar fees are forbidden for landlords.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential rental units in Massachusetts; no exemptions are stated in the text.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit, and locks may be charged before tenancy
rules.penalty: Described as treble damages and attorney's fees in a cited federal case (Perry v. Equity Residential Management, LLC).
rules.ambiguity_note: Text says the law has been in effect since the 1970s but gives no specific date. Source is a secondary landlord-association page describing state law.
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B).

rules.title: Licensed brokers may charge fees to prospective tenants subject to written disclosure
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge fees (including application or screening fees) to prospective tenants. The broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting.
rules.coverage_text: Licensed brokers or salespersons finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee; a landlord acting as own broker is uncertain.
rules.key_value: Written notice of broker fee signed by applicant at first personal meeting
rules.ambiguity_note: Whether a landlord who is also a licensed broker may charge such a fee is unresolved in the text. Secondary source summarizing regulations.
rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – Statewide cap on annual rent increases (blocked from Nov. 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would have capped annual rent increases on covered dwelling units at the lesser of the annual CPI increase or 5%, and repealed the statutory ban on rent control. The SJC ruled in Cella v. Attorney General that it may not appear on the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-facility exemption.
rules.coverage_text: All dwelling units leased for residential (not commercial) use, subject to five exemptions.

exemption_tests.description: Dwelling units in owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units.
Dwelling units whose rents are regulated by a public authority (a mobile housing voucher does not count as regulation).
Dwelling units rented primarily to transient guests for less than 14 consecutive days.
Dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes.
Dwelling units whose first residential certificate of occupancy is less than 10 years old, for 10 years from issuance of the certificate.

rules.exemptions_text: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, publicly regulated units, short-term/transient rentals, facilities operated solely for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes, and units with a certificate of occupancy less than 10 years old.
rules.key_value: Lesser of annual CPI increase or 5%
rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.ambiguity_note: Blog notes proponents may re-file after removing the religious exemption; as of the ruling the petition cannot appear on the Nov. 2026 ballot.

rules.title: Statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts statute broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based upon or implementing rent control, defined to include any regulation requiring below-market rents for residential properties. This ban remains in place because the repeal initiative was blocked.
rules.coverage_text: Statewide prohibition on rent control regulation of residential properties.
rules.quoted_span: .General Laws c. 40P, § 2, "broadly prohibits any regulatoryscheme based upon or implementing rent control."
rules.ambiguity_note: Described by a secondary source discussing a court opinion; enactment date not stated in this chunk.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – statewide rent control (annual increase cap)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would limit annual rent increases for covered residential dwelling units to the lower of the annual CPI increase or five percent. The SJC held the petition violates art. 48's religion exclusion and enjoined placing it on the 2026 ballot.
rules.coverage_text: All dwelling units leased for residential, but not commercial, use, except units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes (concurrence describes it as aimed at large for-profit landlords).
rules.exemptions_text: Dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes.

exemption_tests.description: Dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes
Units leased for commercial rather than residential use
