rules.ambiguity_note: Court remanded for judgment that the petition does not comply with art. 48 and enjoined the Secretary from placing it on the 2026 ballot; the opinion excerpt only partially describes the petition's terms.

rules.title: CORI requested only as final step in application (market rate housing)
rules.requirement: Landlords, property management companies and real estate agents may request standard access CORI on a market-rate housing applicant only as the final step in the application process, and may not use it to screen other household members or buyers/sellers.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords, property management companies, and real estate agents requesting CORI on applicants for market rate housing.
rules.quoted_span:
CORI shall only be requested for a housing applicant as the final step in the application
process.
rules.ambiguity_note: Document footer dated 6/11/21; effective date not explicitly stated.

rules.title: CORI final-step requirement for subsidized housing
rules.requirement: Public housing authorities and property management companies administering subsidized housing may request CORI only as the final step in the application process and must screen only as provided by state and federal law.
rules.coverage_text: Public housing authorities and property management companies administering subsidized housing programs.
rules.quoted_span:
Public housing authorities and property management companies that administer a subsidized
housing program for qualifying subsidized housing units shall screen housing applicants for
subsidized housing only as provided by state and federal law. CORI shall only be requested for
a housing applicant as the final step in the application process.
rules.ambiguity_note: Document footer dated 6/11/21; effective date not explicitly stated.

rules.title: Disclosure of criminal history before questioning or adverse decision
rules.requirement: Landlords, property management companies, real estate agents and public housing authorities must give the applicant a copy of CORI or other criminal history and disclose its source before asking any questions about it and before making an adverse housing decision based on it.

rules.title: Limits on use of CORI to evaluate market-rate and subsidized applicants
rules.requirement: CORI obtained for market-rate housing may be used solely to decide whether to rent or lease to the applicant; CORI obtained for subsidized housing may be used solely to decide qualification for a subsidized program. It may not otherwise be disseminated.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords, property management companies, real estate agents, and public housing authorities.

CORI accessed pursuant to 803 CMR 5.04 by a landlord, property management company,

the housing applicant.

rules.title: Pre-adverse action procedures for CORI-based housing decisions
rules.requirement: Before adverse action based on CORI or criminal history, a landlord, property management company or real estate agent must notify the applicant, provide a copy of the record and source, CORI policy, identify the basis, allow dispute of accuracy, provide DCJIS correction information, and document compliance. rules.title: Requirements for using a consumer reporting agency for CORI
rules.requirement: Before a CRA requests CORI for a housing entity, the entity must register with iCORI, give a separate written notice that a consumer report may be used, obtain separate written authorization, obtain a signed CORI Acknowledgment Form, and certify FCRA compliance to the CRA.

rules.title: Proposed Massachusetts rent control ballot question (struck from November 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide ballot initiative would have limited annual rent increases for residences, with exemptions for several unit types. The Supreme Judicial Court ruled it cannot go on the November ballot because of its religious-use exemption.
rules.coverage_text: Residences generally, except several types of exempt units; details of the cap and the other exemptions are not given in the article.

exemption_tests.description: Units operated solely for religious purposes (among other unspecified exempt unit types).

rules.quoted_span: The proposal limits annual rent increases for residences, but it carved out exemptions for several types of units, including ones “operated solely for … religious … purposes."
rules.ambiguity_note: News summary only. The cap amount and full coverage are not stated. Proponents hinted at a possible 2028 ballot petition.

rules.title: FAIR Act – ban on owners using algorithmic rent-setting software with competitors' nonpublic data
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property owners in New Jersey.

exemption_tests.description: Act does not prohibit certain technologies: spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs.

The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue
management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental
prices.

rules.title: FAIR Act – ban on coordinators facilitating pricing coordination among landlords
rules.requirement: Software providers and other 'coordinators' may not use algorithmic revenue management software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords. A coordinator is anyone operating such software or an algorithmic device that uses nonpublic, competitively sensitive information from multiple residential owners to generate recommendations on rent, lease terms, or occupancy levels.
rules.coverage_text: Software providers and other coordinators serving residential rental property owners in New Jersey.

coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted each year in line with CPI increases, and the Director of Consumer Affairs publishes the adjusted limit.

A licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property.

rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to a dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent, or to a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, up to $750 second offense, up to $1,000 each subsequent offense; the amount wrongfully charged is taken from the penalty and remitted to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.ambiguity_note: Act takes effect on the first day of the fourth month after enactment (approved January 20, 2026); the date 2026-05-01 is derived from that formula and is not stated explicitly in the text.

rules.title: Good cause required to refuse lease renewal (Anti-Eviction Act)
rules.requirement: Landlords of residential rental properties may not fail to renew a written or oral lease unless they have good cause; the good causes are those listed in the eviction section of the guide.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental properties, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted (covered by separate provisions).
Motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units are excepted.

rules.exemptions_text: Owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three 
family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, 
regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.ambiguity_note: Informational guide summarizing the statute; citation appears as written in the guide.

rules.title: Security deposit cap (1.5x monthly rent)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent. Pet deposits combined with the regular deposit, and prepaid rents held as security (including last month's rent), count toward the cap; the landlord may also require the first month's rent at lease inception.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted unless the tenant requests application.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in 30 days after written request to landlord)

rules.exemptions_text: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling, unless tenant sends written request and 30 days pass.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Annual security deposit increase limit (10%)
rules.requirement: Any additional yearly increase of a security deposit may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties under the Security Deposit Law.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.exemptions_text: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling unless tenant requests application.
rules.quoted_span:
Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: 10% of current security deposit per year
rules.ambiguity_note: Citation for this sentence is not stated separately; it follows the cite to N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

rules.title: Deposit must be held in trust in interest-bearing New Jersey account
rules.requirement: Security deposits remain the tenant's property, held in trust and not commingled with the landlord's assets. A landlord receiving deposits for ten or fewer units must place them in an insured New Jersey bank or S&L interest-bearing account; landlords with 10 or more units may use a money market fund or variable-rate account.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rentals under the Security Deposit Law; the holding provision does not apply to seasonal rentals.

exemption_tests.description: Seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days by a person with a permanent residence elsewhere)
Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.exemptions_text: Seasonal use or rental excepted from this section.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must 
deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an 
interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

rules.title: Interest on security deposit belongs to tenant
rules.requirement: Interest or earnings on the deposit belongs to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited toward rent annually.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rentals under the Security Deposit Law.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant

rules.title: Written notice of deposit location within 30 days
rules.requirement: Within 30 days of receiving the deposit, and with each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the bank or investment company, amount, account type and interest rate. If notice or interest is not provided, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% interest to rent after giving written notice.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rentals under the Security Deposit Law.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at t he time of each annual interest 
payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking 
institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, 
type of account, and current rate o f interest for the account.
rules.penalty: Tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days of tenancy termination
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear or money owed under the lease, within 30 days after termination of the tenancy, by personal delivery or registered/certified mail. Failure allows the tenant to sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld plus costs and fees.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rentals under the Security Deposit Law.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees

rules.title: Deposit return within 5 business days when tenant displaced
rules.requirement: When a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, the landlord must return the deposit within five business days and tell the tenant within three business days where it can be collected.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced where an official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified displacement will exceed seven days.
rules.quoted_span:
Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or 
evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: Deposit return within 15 business days after domestic violence lease termination
rules.requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the deposit plus interest available within 15 business days, and give written notice within three business days of when and where it can be picked up, with an itemized list of interest and deductions.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants terminating leases under the New Jersey Safe Housing Act; does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

exemption_tests.description: Transient or seasonal rentals

rules.exemptions_text: This law does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available 
the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s 
agent.

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days after broken lease (timing)
rules.requirement: When a tenant breaks the lease, the landlord's 30-day period to return the security deposit does not begin until the unit is re-rented or the lease expires, whichever occurs first.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies where the tenant breaks the lease agreement.
rules.citation: Truth in Renting (NJ DCA) – security deposit return
rules.quoted_span:
the 30 days that the landlord shall return the tenant’s 
security deposit does not start until the landlord re -rents the rental unit, or until the lease expires, 
whichever occurs first.
rules.key_value: 30 days from re-rental or lease expiry
rules.ambiguity_note: Chunk begins mid-sentence; no statute cited for this passage in this chunk.

rules.title: Deposit return when tenant displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the security deposit within five business days after a tenant is displaced, and within three business days of notice must tell the tenant where to collect it.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation where an official posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified displacement will last longer than seven days.
rules.quoted_span:
Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or 
evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: New owner responsible for security deposit after sale or transfer
rules.requirement: On sale or transfer, the new owner must obtain the deposit and accrued interest from the former owner and is responsible for investing it, giving notices, paying interest and returning it.
rules.coverage_text: Properties sold or transferred.
rules.quoted_span:
If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security 
deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner.

rules.title: Civil penalty for withholding deposit of tenant receiving government assistance
rules.requirement: A landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds the security deposit of a tenant receiving State or federal financial assistance may face a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense; the tenant need not sue to stay in the program.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who have received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may be liable for a civil 
penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.
rules.penalty: Civil penalty of $500–$2,000 per offense

rules.title: Criminal penalty for unlawful use of security deposit monies
rules.requirement: Unlawful use of security deposit monies is a disorderly-person offense punishable by a fine of at least $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment, or both.
rules.coverage_text: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies.
rules.quoted_span:
may be subject to a fine of not less than $200 or imprisonment for not more 
than 30 days, or both (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).
rules.penalty: Disorderly person; fine of not less than $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment, or both

rules.title: Landlord may charge credit report cost and reasonable application fees
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge the tenant the cost of a credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees.
rules.coverage_text: Prospective tenants applying for rental housing.
rules.citation: Truth in Renting (NJ DCA) – Credit Checks and Background Checks
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord is allowed 
to charge the tenant for the cost of the report. The landlord may also request reasonable rental 
application fees or employment verification.
rules.key_value: reasonable application fee; cost of report
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary guidance; no specific statute cited and no dollar cap stated.

rules.title: No statewide rent control; municipalities may adopt rent control
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no state law establishing or controlling rents; municipalities may adopt rent control or leveling ordinances. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion.
rules.coverage_text: Local rent control is determined by municipal ordinance.

exemption_tests.description: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years following completion of construction.
Rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt from local rent control.

rules.quoted_span:
The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents. Municipalities 
may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.
rules.key_value: No state cap; 30-year new construction exemption from local control

rules.title: No mid-lease rent increase; notice required to terminate lease and raise rent
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease term; the old lease must be terminated with proper written notice and a new lease offered at the increased rent.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies under lease.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot raise the 
rent mid-lease term.

rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: Before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase; the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal rent ordinances.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies subject to the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: No rent increase to cover conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion; increases for new services or amenities remain allowed.
rules.coverage_text: All tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act – good cause required to evict or refuse to renew
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a lease (written or oral) without good cause, and must prove in court that statutory grounds exist. Possession may be recovered only by consent or through court eviction process; each cause other than nonpayment must be described in a written notice, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good-cause evictions except nonpayment.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in mobile home parks, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.

exemption_tests.description: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.

Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (hotel/motel occupants with no alternate residence who live there continually are covered).
Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of an immediate family member who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the unit.

rules.exemptions_text: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units; hotel/motel/guest house transient or seasonal guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; statutory grounds include nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, breach of rules or lease covenants, failure to pay a rent increase, and health/safety or removal from rental market.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.ambiguity_note: Exemption text is internally unclear ("two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units"). Source is a state agency summary publication.

rules.title: Eviction ground: permanent removal of property from rental market for redevelopment/blight clearance (relocation assistance)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict where a governmental agency wants to permanently take the property off the rental market for redevelopment or clearing blighted land. Three months' Notice to Quit is required and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Law (coverage rules stated elsewhere in the document).
rules.quoted_span: The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.ambiguity_note: Chunk begins mid-section; the opening of the ground is in the prior chunk.

rules.title: Eviction ground: permanently retiring property from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord permanently retiring a building or mobile home park from residential use may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing; no action until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use.
rules.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction ground: refusal of reasonable lease changes
rules.requirement: At lease expiration a landlord may propose reasonable but substantial lease changes; if the tenant refuses after written notice, the landlord may sue and the court decides reasonableness. One month's Notice to Quit is required.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law; landlord bears burden of proof for protected tenancies.
rules.quoted_span:
If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those 
changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed 
changes are reasonable.

rules.title: Eviction ground: continuous non-payment or habitual late payment of rent
rules.requirement: After a written Notice to Cease, a landlord may sue to evict a tenant who continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late. One month's Notice to Quit is required.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction ground: conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple
rules.requirement: A landlord converting property to condo, co-op or fee simple of two or more units may sue for eviction after a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing, with stays of eviction available and protection for senior/disabled protected tenants.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of two or more units or sites.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord must comply with the regulations 
governing conversion to condominiums and cooperatives, before a warrant for possession 
shall be issued.
rules.key_value: 3 years' Notice to Quit; up to five one-year stays

rules.title: Eviction ground: sale to owner-occupant after conversion (tenancy began after master deed)
rules.requirement: Owner of a building being converted may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the master deed was recorded if the unit is sold to a buyer who will personally occupy it and the contract calls for vacancy; tenant must have been given a conversion statement; two months' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose initial tenancy began after the master deed, cooperative agreement or subdivision plat was recorded.
rules.quoted_span:
However, no action 
shall be brought against a tenant under paragraph one (1) of this subsection unless the 
tenant was given a statement, informing the tenant that the property is being converted.

rules.title: Eviction ground: owner of three or fewer condo/co-op units seeking personal occupancy or sale
rules.requirement: Owner of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units may evict a tenant whose rental began after the master deed was recorded if the owner will personally occupy or has contracted to sell to a buyer who will occupy; two months' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of three or less condominium or 
cooperative units seeks to evict a tenant whose initial tenancy began, by rental, after the 
master deed or agreement establishing the cooperative was recorded, because the owner 
seeks to personally occupy the unit, or has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks 
to personally occupy it and the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time 
of closing.

rules.title: Eviction ground: owner of building with three or fewer units seeking personal occupancy or sale
rules.requirement: Owner of a building with three residential units or less may evict to personally occupy a unit or to deliver it vacant to a buyer who will occupy it; two months' Notice to Quit and no action until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with three residential units or less.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building with three residential units 
or less seeks to personally occupy a unit, or has contracted to sell the residential unit to a 
buyer who wishes to personally occupy it and the contract fo r sale calls for the unit to be 
vacant at the time of closing.

rules.title: Eviction ground: termination of employment-based tenancy
rules.requirement: Where a tenant lives in the property on condition of employment by the landlord and the employment is terminated, the landlord may sue for eviction after a three-day Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing in the property as a condition of employment.
rules.quoted_span:
If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction ground: drug offense conviction on the property
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant convicted of or pleading guilty to drug offenses on the property (unless in rehabilitation), or who lets such a person occupy the premises; suit must be brought within two years; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior 
to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).

rules.title: Eviction ground: conviction for assault or terrorist threats against landlord, family or employees
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant convicted of assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, family or employees, or who permits such a person to reside there; suit within two years; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, 
or if a juvenile has been found by the court to be delinquent due to an offense involving 
assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landl ord’s family or an 
employee of the landlord.

rules.title: Eviction ground: civil court finding of liability for theft, assault or drug activity
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant found liable in a civil proceeding for theft on the premises, assault or terrorist threats against the landlord's side, or illegal drug activity on the premises; suit within two years; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant is found by a civil court proceeding (not 
criminal) to be liable fo r involvement in theft of property located on the premises

rules.title: Eviction ground: conviction for theft of property
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant convicted of theft from the landlord or other tenants in the building, or who permits such a person to reside there; three days' Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, 
or if a juvenile has been found to be delinquent by the Court due to an offense involving 
theft of property from the landlord or from tenants residing in the same building or 
complex.

rules.title: Eviction ground: human trafficking violation
rules.requirement: A landlord may sue to evict a tenant found in a civil action to have committed human trafficking violations on the premises or to have harbored a person engaged in human trafficking; action must be brought within two years after the violation ends.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span:
No action for 
removal pursuant to this subsection may be brought mor e than two years after the alleged 
violation has terminated (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(r)).

rules.title: Evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings may be removed only by court order, and the landlord must prove one of the listed causes (holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, willful damage, constant rule violations, lease violation with re-entry right). Notice-to-quit periods vary by cause and tenancy type.
rules.coverage_text: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span:
Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when 
a court issues an order for eviction.
rules.key_value: 3-day, 1-month or 3-month notice to quit depending on cause/tenancy

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions follow Eviction Law good cause
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good cause and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau, and give three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction.
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses.

exemption_tests.description: Hotels with more than 85 percent temporary occupancy, school and college dormitories, buildings housing only college students and certain residences for the disabled are excepted from rooming/boarding house definition.

rules.quoted_span:
The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the 
Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, 
require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements 
of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 
5:27-3.3(c)).
rules.key_value: 3 working days' notice to County Welfare Board

rules.title: Penalty: landlord must occupy unit six months after personal-occupancy eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord who gets a unit vacated by giving notice of personal occupancy must occupy it for at least six months; otherwise liable to the former tenant for three times damages plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants vacating after notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord 
wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.
rules.penalty: Three times damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs

rules.title: Penalty: five-year bar on residential use after removal/retirement notice
rules.requirement: After a tenant vacates following notice of permanent board-up, demolition or retirement from residential use, the property may not be used residentially for five years; violations bring treble damages, fees and a civil penalty.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants vacating after notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up, demolish or retire the building from residential use.
rules.quoted_span:
When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks 
to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, 
the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.
rules.key_value: 5 years; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000.00 per violation

rules.title: Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction; 90-day notice to quit for owner-occupant buyer
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction; a buyer of a foreclosed property who wants to occupy it as a primary residence must give a 90-day notice to quit and wait until any lease expires. Month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units are not exempt.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenants in foreclosed properties.
rules.quoted_span:
Before a tenant can be evicted due 
to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the 
foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her 
primary residence.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy (condominium/cooperative conversion)
rules.requirement: Eligible senior, disabled, or disabled-veteran tenants living in a building at least one year before its conversion to condominium/cooperative/fee simple may be protected from eviction for 40 years if family income does not exceed the stated limit. Landlords/converters must notify tenants of their right to apply, and applications are generally due within 60 days.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants aged 62+, permanently disabled, or honorably discharged veterans disabled at 60%+, residing in a building at least one year before conversion recording date.
rules.key_value: 40 years protection; income not more than 3x county average per-person income or $50,000, whichever is greater
rules.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act of 1992 (Hudson County conversions)
rules.requirement: Extends conversion-related protected tenancy to qualified tenants in qualified counties (currently only Hudson County) who were not eligible as senior citizens or disabled persons.
rules.coverage_text: Qualified tenants in buildings converted or being converted in Hudson County who were not eligible under the 1981 Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act.
rules.quoted_span:
At 
the present time, the only qualified county is Hudson County (N.J.A.C. 5:24-3.2(b)).
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary page; the text does not specify the scope of the protections.

rules.title: LAD source-of-lawful-income discrimination ban (Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment, e.g. they cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder the right to rent solely because of that income source.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to the sale or rental of all property under the NJ Law Against Discrimination, except listed owner-occupied and religious-organization exemptions.
rules.exemptions_text: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms by an owner/occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference for persons of the same religion; housing for older persons exemption applies only to familial status.

exemption_tests.description: Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling, the other unit of which is occupied by the owner as residence.
Rental of a room or rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied by him/her as residence.
Preference given to persons of the same religion by a religious organization in sale, lease or rental of real property.

rules.citation: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm referenced; NJ Division on Civil Rights brochure
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.

rules.title: FAIR Act: ban on rental property owners using a coordinator's services

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. Just cause is either at-fault (e.g., nonpayment, breach, nuisance, criminal activity) or no-fault (owner/relative move-in for 12 months, withdrawal from rental market, government/court orders, demolition or substantial remodel), with no-fault grounds requiring good faith, notice contents and re-offer/relocation obligations.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property with a tenancy of more than 30 days in San Diego, except listed exemptions (including housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years).
rules.exemptions_text: Transient/tourist hotels, short-term occupancy, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under the MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities and transitional housing, dormitories, shared-facility rooms with resident landlord, owner-occupied single-family residences, owner-occupied duplexes, housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, and separately alienable property owned by non-corporate/non-REIT landlords with written notice.
